reason: The cited evidence (E1) demonstrates improved CO oxidation and stability for high-entropy spinel oxides, but it concerns earth-abundant first-row transition metals, not atomically dispersed PGMs on fluorite supports. None of the key premises about PGM stabilization, Pd–O–M bonding, or HEFO-specific mechanisms are directly supported by this evidence.
premises: High-entropy fluorite oxide (HEFO) supports can stabilize atomically dispersed PGMs via strong Pd–O–M bonds.
The diversified cationic environment in HEFO enhances lattice oxygen reducibility and weakens inhibitory species chemisorption.
HEFO-supported catalysts will show lower CO oxidation onset temperature (~80 °C) compared to Pt/CeO2.
HEFO-supported catalysts will exhibit enhanced durability and suppressed PGM sintering under thermal cycling.
The proposed mechanism and performance improvements are supported by prior evidence on high-entropy oxides.
